subject: POC trial success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@atlaspayments.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the proposed POC/trial success criteria, the evaluation plan, timelines, and ownership so we have a shared checklist going into the next steps. Please review and flag anything that needs to change.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms (note: will call out peak vs steady-state below)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s for production steady state; ability to handle 500 req/s for batch run during reconciliation windows
- Cost: target gross cost <= $0.0005 per token (model + infra estimate)
- Quality: response acceptance/accuracy >= 90% on our evaluation set; hallucination rate < 2%

Evaluation plan (what we'll test):
1) Functional quality: we will run our annotated test set (N=1,200 prompts) against the candidate model and measure precision/recall/acceptance metrics.
2) Latency/throughput: run synthetic load tests reflective of peak traffic and steady-state traffic. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and end-to-end SLA breakpoints.
3) Cost profiling: capture tokens consumed per workflow and end-to-end cost per transaction.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: kickoff + environment access (we provide a temporary trial config)
- Week 1: ingest eval dataset + baseline runs (quality + perf)
- Week 2: optimizations (quantization / batching / cache tuning) + rerun measurements
- Week 3: final validation and handoff + decision/recommendation

Ownership:
- Jordan Blake (Redwood): commercial lead, deal/procurement and overall timeline owner
- Marissa Cole (Redwood): technical owner for eval harness, test runs, and results collations
- Marcus Lin (Redwood): runtime tuning / infra points of contact
- Atlas: Tom (tech) and Aisha (procurement/stakeholder) to provide production traffic patterns and procurement timeline

Next steps:
- I'll share the trial evaluation plan (attached) and a short SOW draft for procurement.
- Can Atlas confirm target start week (we suggested week of Mar 8) and primary technical owner?
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff with Tom + Marissa + Marcus next week to walk through test harness and required access/keys.

Attachments: trial-eval-plan.xlsx

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

--
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC trial success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Tom and ops: 
- Latency: for our peak reconciliation windows we need p95 <= 250ms. Steady-state 300ms is acceptable but peak must hit 250ms.
- Throughput: our expected production steady-state is ~200 req/s but during batch reconciliation we will need to sustain ~500 req/s for short bursts (10-20 minutes).
- Cost: procurement will want a 90-day run-rate estimate; can you provide a cost/token and a projected monthly estimate based on our volume?

Also, procurement will need a short SOW and SOC 2 executive summary to start the security review. Tom will be the primary technical owner; ops@atlaspayments.com should be included for access details.

We can start the trial week of Mar 8 but procurement will need the SOW this week to keep timelines. Can you send updated plan + SOW and SOC2 summary?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product Operations | Atlas Payments
aisha.khan@atlaspayments.com

Adjustments based on your feedback: 
- Latency: set p95 <= 250ms for peak reconciliation windows; steady-state p95 <= 300ms. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 across both load profiles.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 req/s; batch reconciliation bursts up to 500 req/s (we'll run a dedicated load test to validate autoscaling and queueing behavior).
- Cost: preliminary estimate ~ $0.00045 / token based on projected model selection and expected batching savings. We'll run a 90-day projection once we have exact volume numbers.
- Quality: baseline pass threshold is 90% acceptance on your annotated set; we will provide confusion/hallucination metrics as part of the report.

Proposed firm timeline: trial start Mar 8, 2026 — 3 week active testing window, with final validation week ending Mar 29. If procurement needs more lead time we can delay start by one week but we'd like to keep Mar 8 as target.

Owners (confirmed): Jordan — procurement & timeline; Marissa — test harness and test runs (will coordinate with Tom); Marcus — runtime tuning + infra monitoring.

- Atlas to confirm start week and provide sample traffic CSV + estimated volume for cost projection.
